split_strategies.proof_of_KEventDelete_return_wit_1_split: Pure target, no spatial resources or existential. PreH3 gives safeExec (LastSeen looked_up) (ret 0) (kevent_delete_lookup_cont id_pre X). Open safeExec, retain the same semantic-state witness and LastSeen fact, use wp_ret to obtain the continuation at pointer 0, unfold kevent_delete_lookup_cont and reduce Z.eqb 0 0. This is weakestpre (ret tt) X at that same state; reconstruct safeExec. No transition of looked_up or new heap resource is required.

split_strategies.proof_of_KEventDelete_which_implies_wit_: Pure target, no spatial resources. PreH1 supplies safeExec (LastSeen before) (abs_event_delete id) X. Open safeExec and retain its state witness and LastSeen fact. Unfold abs_event_delete into bind (abs_find_event id) (fun p => if Z.eqb p 0 then ret tt else abs_event_delete_at id p); wp_bind changes weakestpre of this bind into weakestpre of abs_find_event under the continuation. Fold kevent_delete_lookup_cont and rebuild safeExec using the same source state. Use the imported MonadErrHoare.wp_bind equality pointwise; no extra guard or helper premise is needed.

Pure target, no spatial resources. PreH2 supplies safeExec (LastSeen looked_up) (ret event) (kevent_delete_lookup_cont id X). Preserve its semantic-state witness and LastSeen fact, use wp_ret, and unfold the continuation. PreH1 event <> 0 proves Z.eqb event 0 = false. The remaining weakestpre is abs_event_delete_at id event under X; rebuild safeExec at the same looked_up state. This exposes the pending deletion, without asserting any post-deletion state.
